          Roma 3-4 Real Madrid Stats: Rüdiger Completes Seven-Minute Comeback in Champions League Thriller
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Joel Sritharan / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Roma seemed to be heading for a famous victory over Real Madrid in the Champions League, but José Mourinho's men had other ideas.
Antonio Rüdiger and José Mourinho came back to haunt Roma as Real Madrid scored three goals in seven minutes late on to claim a thrilling 4-3 Champions League win.
Los Blancos were trailing 3-1 before Carlos Espí struck in the 83rd minute.
From there, Endrick and former Roma defender Rüdiger completely flipped the script at Stadio Olimpico as Mourinho got one over on his old club.

Roma, encouraged by a roaring home crowd, made a fast start as Matías Soulé curled narrowly wide after just 48 seconds before Mario Hermoso's curling effort was tipped away by Thibaut Courtois at full stretch.

Paulo Dybala poked wide from Nahuel Molina's cutback, and though Roma received a blow when Manu Koné was forced off with an injury, they took a deserved lead when Marten de Roon‘s first-time strike from outside the box was deflected past Courtois in the 20th minute.

However, Madrid equalised against the run of play as Kylian Mbappé, on his 100th Champions League appearance, capitalised on an error from Hermoso before lashing past Pierluigi Gollini, bringing up his 500th goal involvement in club football in the process (378 goals, 122 assists).

Jude Bellingham missed a huge opportunity before half-time, sweeping past the right post, and it looked to be costly when Donyell Malen scored twice in six second-half minutes; he first beat Courtois at the near post after a brilliant pass from Rodrigo Mora, while his second was a routine finish following a clever pass from Soule.
Mbappé had a goal disallowed after the hour-mark, but substitutes Espi and Endrick swung the tide.
Endrick's initial header from a corner was kept out by Gollini, but Espí was on hand to tap in the rebound.
Roma were undone again two minutes later when Endrick headed in unchallenged from Arda Güler's corner, and Rüdiger had the final say as he volleyed past Gollini in the 90th minute.
Mourinho was asked about Endrick's lack of minutes in his pre-match press conference and the Portuguese insisted the youngster has a bright future at the club, which was perhaps proven by this cameo.
The Brazilian's two shots proved crucial, with the first leading to Espí's goal and the quickfire second giving Madrid hope of snatching all three points rather than settling for just a point.

While Endrick, Espí and Rüdiger will take most of the headlines, it was another substitute in Güler who was the unsung hero. His two assists were crucial as his pinpoint crossing proved to be the difference in the end.

Only Lamine Yamal (40), Michael Olise (36) and Florian Thauvin (33) have created more chances in Europe's top five leagues this season than Güler (31), who will surely regain his starting position in Mourinho's team now.
Endrick, though, will likely have to still settle for a role as a super-sub, given he is behind Mbappé in the pecking order.

Mbappé became the youngest player to reach a century of European Cup/Champions League games, aged 27 years and 298 days, surpassing the record previously held by Lionel Messi (28 years, 84 days in 2015).

The France superstar became the eighth player to mark their 100th appearance in the competition with a goal, and the third to do so while playing for Madrid, after Cristiano Ronaldo in 2014 and Toni Kroos in 2019.
